newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close higher, buoyed by bonds.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close higher, buoyed by bonds.

text.p: French shares closed higher on Wednesday in robust volume, bolstered by firm bonds, strength on Wall Street and buying by U.S. investors, traders said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 18.63 points at 2,141.84 with most shares in the index posting gains. But the CAC-40 futures contract ended two points lower at 2,149.0.
"With 10-year interest rates at six percent, it's good for shares," one trader said. But he cautioned that a "healthy" consolidation could be in store.

One trader said the market also benefited on Wednesday from asset switches to Europe from Japan by U.S. investors interested in cyclical stocks. Another said: "Americans are starting to realise that monetary union is really going to happen" which would favour a low interest rate climate.
Defence manufacturer Thomson CSF ended up 2.95 percent at 157.0 francs on market sentiment that Alcatel Alsthom or Lagardere could offer a relatively high price for the group.
Alcatel Alsthom ended 0.52 percent lower at 436.50 francs despite upward revisions to profit forecasts by brokerages.
Castorama ended down 5.47 percent at 899 francs after warnings analysts that it lacked the foreign growth needed to compensate for regulatory curbs on domestic expansion.
Primagaz was among top gainers, soaring 9.65 percent after it reported half profit climbed 21 percent. It forecast a 10 to 15 percent increase in full year profits.

Debt-laden Anglo-French channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc announced a deal in principle with creditors on a financial restructuring. A source close to the dossier said trade in Eurotunnel shares should resume trade by Tuesday at latest. The shares were suspended at 9.05 francs on Monday.
Holding Suez finished up 0.73 percent at 206.50 francs in volume of 539,484 shares. The volume was swollen by a block trade of 294,000 shares at 205 francs.
Bank CIC ended 2.96 percent higher at 383.0 francs after its half year net profit rocketed 60.5 percent, beating many analysts' foreasts.

Drugs company Sanofi finished up 3.72 percent at 452.20 francs, building on Wednesday's gains after the announcement that it and Bristol Myers Squibb had filed regulatory applications in the United States and European Union for market approval of new hypertension drug irbesartan.
Utility Generale des Eaux up 1.80 percent after giving analysts an upbeat outlook for its new telecoms venture.
